chapter: Publishing, Jelly Roll in Los Angeles and band lore
title: Pops Woodward is really William Woodman
summary: The partner Jelly Roll names was trombonist Woodman, father of Britt Woodman, who put in the most money when the band bought the hall.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: He doesn't ever mention Dink Johnson in this part of the book so I didn't realize that it was all the same Johnson family. And so who was Pops Woodward?
Pops Woodward. I think he was a bass player around here at that time. I...uh, yeah.
This says trombone player. Is that right?
Woodward. Pops Woodward. He went partners with Pops Woodward to open the Wayside Park at Leek's Lake.

Well, that's Woodman he's talkin' about. Woodman was a trombone player. But there was an old man around here was playin' fiddle, I think--bass violin--I think his name was Woodward, too, but you see, I told you, when I sold out my place, I sold it out to the musicians--Woodman was one of them. Woodman and...uh, I don't know...who they all were...seven or eight of them. Jesse Smith was one, and Everett Walsh, I think, was one. I don't remember...
So what he did, when he said he went into partnerships with Woodward, what he did was, he went into partnerships with William Woodman and some other musicians. I see.
But I think Woodman had most of the money. Woodman was pretty close, you know. He saved his money, and I think he had more money in there than any of 'em.
And he's the one who's the father of Britt Woodman and Brother Woodman and...
